source.title: A Convergence Theory Towards Practical Over-parameterized Deep Neural Networks
source.authors: Asaf Noy; Yi Xu; Yonathan Aflalo; Lihi Zelnik-Manor; Rong Jin

record.tranche_reason: The study reports training outcomes for randomly initialized ReLU networks using regression loss on CIFAR-10 and SGEMM, a different measure and setup from the listed claim versions.
record.gate_note: The paper also cites prior findings about memorizing random labels and spurious minima; those cited results are not rows. Its CIFAR-10 experiment converts classification labels to one-hot regression targets and reports MSE, not classification error.
record.test_reason: The study reports fully connected regression results and guarantees for training a fixed-gate surrogate. None tests V1–V6: CIFAR-10 squared loss is not training classification error, the width experiments do not identify spurious minima in two-layer teacher-student networks, and there are no shortcut, initialization, stability-threshold or batch-normalization comparisons.
record.authors_conclusion: The record is broadly accurate. More precisely, the authors derive improved width and iteration guarantees for their GReLU training scheme and assert a transformation to an equivalent ReLU network on the training set. Experiments support faster optimization in the tested regression settings. These guarantees should not be paraphrased as guarantees for ordinary gradient descent directly on standard ReLU networks. SGD, cross-entropy, convolutional networks and residual networks are described as extensions.
record.recipe_differences: The theory and experiments use fully connected regression with squared loss and batch gradient descent; GReLU additionally fixes randomized activation patterns during training. The CIFAR-10 classification task is converted to one-hot regression.
record.method_sensitivity: Width changes the synthetic-task convergence outcome; on SGEMM, learning rate, width, and depth are varied, and greater width and depth improve results. On CIFAR-10, reported architectures differ in depth and width; all listed ReLU training MSE values remain above zero.

fits_no_version.finding: On CIFAR-10 one-hot regression, the three ReLU architectures have losses 0.48, 0.27 and 0.75; paired GReLU networks have losses 0.02, 0.01 and 0.03.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Fixed-gate GReLU training reaches lower squared training loss than paired fully connected ReLU networks in the tested CIFAR-10 setup.

fits_no_version.finding: For both network types, all five synthetic-regression runs at m = n^2 L reach zero error, while none at the tested lower widths converge within the experiment.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Width affects finite-run convergence on the tested four-layer synthetic regression task; the outcome does not establish trapping in spurious local minima.

fits_no_version.finding: Neither network reaches zero loss on SGEMM. At larger learning rates, GReLU losses decrease more monotonically and reach lower values than ReLU losses.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Fixed-gate GReLU improves regression optimization relative to paired ReLU networks in the tested SGEMM learning-rate experiments.

record.problems: CIFAR-10 is evaluated as one-hot regression and the table reports MSE rather than classification error. Synthetic experiments use only 5 random seeds. The SGEMM findings are described in text alongside figures, without numeric loss values in the supplied text. Experiments use batch gradient descent and fully connected networks, limiting transfer to other optimizers and architectures.
record.rows_left_out: No additional eligible outcomes were omitted. Figure-only trajectories without explicit textual outcomes were not extracted as numeric rows.

untested.parts: Convolutional-network training classification error on CIFAR-10/100 under SGD or Adam, including random or corrupted labels and the smaller-model, stopping and regularization conditions.
Spurious-minimum frequencies in two-layer ReLU teacher-student problems, joint teacher/student growth, and adding one or two student neurons.
Training degradation with depth in plain batch-normalized convolutional networks, its prevention by identity shortcuts, and the specified tanh and Fixup alternatives.
Effects of activation-matched initialization on training speed and depth, including matched-variance orthogonal-versus-Gaussian comparisons and orthogonal convolution kernels.
Loss and curvature dynamics relative to the initial linearized stability limit, edge-of-stability behavior, and divergence from below the threshold.
Training speed and learning-rate tolerance with versus without batch normalization, including the Fixup alternative.

record.verdict_notes: The extracted relation and tranche should change from tests/T2 to discusses/T6. The paper cites original findings relevant to the versions, but its own results fit none. States are cannot_determine relative to V1–V6; this does not dispute the reported regression outcomes. The authors acknowledge that much smaller learning rates might allow narrower synthetic-task networks to converge.

versions.untested_parts: The study does not report CIFAR-10 or CIFAR-100 training classification error, corrupted or random labels, Adam, or the listed small-model, early-stopping, and regularization comparisons.
No two-layer teacher-student neuron-count sweep or spurious-minimum outcome is tested.
No plain-versus-identity-shortcut depth comparison is tested; GReLU fixed gates are not residual identity shortcuts.
No comparison of the listed activation-matched, Gaussian, or orthogonal initializations is tested.
No stability-limit learning-rate sweep or sharpness measurement is reported.

relation.reason: The paper discusses fitting labels, spurious minima, residual connections, and batch normalization, while its own results address a different optimization setting.

tranche.reason: Fully connected squared-loss regression and fixed-gate convergence guarantees do not test V1–V6. No teacher-student spurious-minimum, shortcut, initialization comparison, stability-threshold, or batch-normalization test is reported.

source_check.notes: The paper calls its summed squared-error objective MSE; these values are not training classification errors. Truncated width descriptions were checked only as visible: Section 6.1 specifies lower widths m=(n^2 L)^p with p<1 and m=nL, and allows that smaller learning rates might permit narrower networks to converge.
